minutes.headline: Open Space Committee agreed not to change its Parmenter/Reservoir Road request despite a new Shady Point access offer.
minutes.summary: The committee approved January minutes, heard a report on the 17 February joint site visits, and discussed a new Shady Point offer of free resident access to Lake Shirley that is contingent on the select board not transferring care and control to Parks. Members declined to change their recommendation until they see the offer in writing, and Parks will appear before the select board first. Planning raised a possible Chapter 61 problem with an approved ANR at 100 Howard Street, and a resident spoke about the old Primary School field and T-ball.

public_comment.topic: Select board is deciding T-ball use of the old Primary School field; he argues the town charter gives the town manager authority over town property use, and prefers leaving town land in least restrictive status.

votes.motion: Approve the January 10, 2024 minutes as distributed

passed (roll call: Brandon, Anna, Mary, Matt aye and the chair aye)

budget_items.what_was_said: Parks said funding was not going to be completed at this town meeting and the Land and Water Conservation grant result is still unknown. If the grant is awarded, Parks will seek funding at a special town meeting.
The Parks speaker was disappointed with the budget, saying debt falling off stays inside the operating budget rather than being excluded, which makes open space and recreation projects hard to fund.

budget_items.topic: ARPA-funded Marshall Park work and owner's project manager RFQ
budget_items.what_was_said: An RFQ for an owner's project manager will be paid from grant and ARPA money, with a goal of breaking ground in summer for the pavilion, playground and courts.

Two active grants on conservation land: one involving the snow riders and a Mass Trails-funded ATV groomer, and one for engineered parking plans at three areas that is on the back burner for lack of staff time.

decisions.decision: Members agreed not to change the committee's recommendation to the select board on Parmenter/Reservoir Road care and control until the Shady Point offer is seen in writing.
Parks and Recreation to appear before the select board first; the chair will check with the select board's office about the agenda.
Next meetings set for March 13th and April 10th.
Planning's member will try, through the chair, to float joint meeting dates with the planning board on the 100 Howard Street right of first refusal issue.
Members recommended that the planning board seek town counsel's opinion on the ANR at 100 Howard Street still in Chapter 61.

what_happened.line: The Open Space Committee agreed not to change its Parmenter/Reservoir Road recommendation until a new Shady Point access offer is seen in writing.
Parks and Recreation is to appear before the select board first; the chair will check with the select board's office about the agenda.
Members recommended that the planning board seek town counsel's opinion on an approved ANR at 100 Howard Street that is still in Chapter 61.
Parks said Marshall Park funding will not be completed at this town meeting; a special town meeting follows only if the Land and Water Conservation grant is awarded.
Next meetings were set for March 13th and April 10th.

why_it_matters: Whether Lake Shirley access for residents is offered free depends on a condition about who holds care and control of the land, and that offer is not yet in writing, so the recommendation to the select board has not moved.
Marshall Park's playground, pavilion and courts depend on a grant decision and possibly a special town meeting vote, so residents may be asked to vote on funding outside the annual town meeting.
A possible Chapter 61 problem at 100 Howard Street bears on whether the town's right of first refusal on that land was properly handled.
watch_next: Next Open Space Committee meetings on March 13th and April 10th.
Parks and Recreation's appearance before the select board, and any joint meeting with the planning board on 100 Howard Street.
